ledger.note: 1358: the Treaty of Zadar forces Venice to give up Dalmatia and the Republic of Ragusa is established under Hungarian overlordship. Infobox 'Established: 1358'; 'the Treaty of Zadar forced Venice to yield all claims to Dalmatia'; 'On 27 May 1358, the final agreement was reached at Visegrád'. The page names the city and, from earlier dates, Ston and Pelješac (1333) and Lastovo, not a boundary.

region.text: the Primorje strip between Ragusa and Pelješac

ledger.note: 1399: Ragusa acquires the Primorje coast. 'In 1399, the city acquired the area between Ragusa and Pelješac.' The page does not name the previous holder; Bosnia is the researcher's reading from the war with Bosnia of 1403-1404 that followed.

region.text: the Primorje strip between Ragusa and Pelješac

ledger.note: 1403: war with Bosnia over the Primorje. 'A brief war with Bosnia in 1403 and 1404 ended with Bosnian withdrawal.'

region.text: the Primorje strip between Ragusa and Pelješac

ledger.note: 1404: the war ends with the Bosnian withdrawal; Ragusa keeps the Primorje.

1419: Ragusa buys eastern Konavle from Sandalj Hranic. 'the Republic of Ragusa came into possession of the eastern part of Konavle' 'on June 24, 1419, by a purchase and sale agreement'; the page says Konavle was 'part of Bosnia in the hands of powerful feudal lords'.

region.text: the western part of Konavle, with Cavtat and Obod

ledger.note: 1426: Ragusa buys western Konavle, with Cavtat and Obod, from Radoslav Pavlovic. 'on December 31, 1426, the Ragusans purchased the remaining western part of Konavle'; 'its final borders were formed by 1426' (S6).

1451: Herceg Stjepan attacks Ragusa for Konavle and besieges Dubrovnik. 'In 1451, Stjepan attacked the Republic of Ragusa in order to gain the region of Konavle' and 'laid siege to the city of Dubrovnik'.
1454: peace with the duke; Ragusa keeps Konavle. 'the peace with Dubrovnik was concluded in 1454'.

region.text: the City and Republic of Ragusa, of which General Lauriston took possession

ledger.note: 1806: French troops occupy the republic. Infobox 'Invasion by France: 26 May 1806'; 'General Lauriston took possession of the City and Republic of Ragusa, on the 27th of May'; overlord 'First French Empire (1806-1808)'. Added by reviewer eu-18-f: the owner records the occupation with the roles reversed (schema).

region.text: the republic's territory, entered by the Russian and Montenegrin forces

ledger.note: 1806: Russians and Montenegrins besiege French-held Ragusa. Infobox 'Date: 27 May - 1 October 1806, French victory'; 'Russian and Montenegrin troops entered Ragusan territory and began fighting the French army' (S1); General Lauriston took possession of the city on 27 May (S1).
1806: General Molitor appears in their rear and the Russian-Montenegrin forces abandon the siege; the siege period ends 1 October.

region.text: the republic, annexed when the occupation ends

ledger.note: 1808: the occupation ends in annexation. 'In 1808, Marshal Marmont issued a proclamation abolishing the Republic of Ragusa'; infobox 'Annexation by Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy: 31 January 1808'. Added by reviewer eu-18-f.

1808: Marshal Marmont abolishes the Republic of Ragusa. 'In 1808, Marshal Marmont issued a proclamation abolishing the Republic of Ragusa'; infobox 'Annexation ... 31 January 1808'; the French had held it since 27 May 1806.

wars.name: Ragusan-Bosnian war of 1403-1404

zones.text: the Primorje strip between Ragusa and Pelješac

wars.outcome: 'ended with Bosnian withdrawal'; Ragusa kept the area between the city and Pelješac acquired in 1399.

wars.name: First Konavle War
belligerents: the Bosnian lords of Konavle (opponent not named on the page)
wars.outcome: 'The First Konavle War lasted from 1430 to 1433'; the page does not say how it ended. Konavle stayed Ragusan ('envoys declared before the Ottoman sultan in 1430 that Konavle was actually the property of Ragusa').

wars.name: War of Herceg Stjepan against Ragusa
wars.outcome: Stjepan Vukcic besieged Dubrovnik; the Ragusan government declared him a traitor; peace in 1454; Konavle stayed Ragusan.

wars.name: Siege of Ragusa (1806)
wars.outcome: 'French victory': the Russian-Montenegrin forces abandoned the siege after Molitor appeared in their rear; France abolished the republic in 1808.
wars.note: The disambiguation page Siege of Ragusa (S9) lists the 866-868 Aghlabid siege, 1806, 1814 and 1991-92 sieges; the 1814 Anglo-Austrian siege of the French-held city is not opened.

certainty.note: The Primorje and Konavle frontiers with Bosnia are not fixed by a dated line until the purchases; Ston and Pelješac come from a 1325 sale and 1333 handover.
'Its final borders were formed by 1426'; the land frontier is fixed by purchase deeds and, from the 1699 Treaty of Karlowitz, by the two Ottoman buffer corridors at Neum and Sutorina.

notes:
Cliopatria rows: the republic is drawn from 1385 though established 1358; the five-cell outline (1,540 km2, all inside the gazetteer's Herzegovina cells) omits the Pelješac peninsula, Mljet and Lastovo, so every keyframe is an adjust that adds a Pelješac circle and a Mljet circle (about one cell each). Neither the republic's page nor Konavle gives an area.
Overlordship, not territory: Hungary 1358-1458, the Ottoman Empire 1458-1684 (tribute treaty 1458, 'defined at 12,500 gold coins' in 1481), Habsburg Austria 1684-1806, the First French Empire 1806-1808 are infobox statuses. The ottoman-empire dossier should hold a vassal_start for 1458 with counterpart republic-of-ragusa, and the kingdom-of-hungary dossier a 1358-1458 relation; the page also dates short-term Ottoman arrangements to 1430 and 1442. The first-french-empire dossier should hold the occupation_start of 27 May 1806 with counterpart republic-of-ragusa.
Not recorded as ledger events: the 1699 cession of the Neum and Sutorina corridors (S11 and S6: 'Neum and Sutorina were attached to Sanjak of Herzegovina'), because Neum shares an H3 cell with Ston and the gazetteer grid cannot show it; Klek was 'usurped' by the Ottomans after 1718 without a date; Cliopatria's 1772 polygon refinement has no event. Lastovo and Mljet have no acquisition dates on the pages. The Ragusan 1814 siege (Anglo-Austrian, S9 lists it) was not opened; Cliopatria ends the row in 1808.
Gazetteer names needed: Konavle, Pelješac, Ston, Mljet, Lastovo, Cavtat, Neum, Sutorina, Župa dubrovačka.
